case_name: VANKO — Insider Threat / IP Exfiltration (Stark Enterprises, 2016)
description: FOR500 case. Anthony Vanko, lead biochemical engineer at Stark Enterprises DC R&D Facility, suspected of exfiltrating classified research (zebrafish DNA, rapid cell regeneration, weaponization research) to a Chinese university server. Evidence: Microsoft Surface 3 (119GB physical EWF image, FTK Imager 2.9, examiner Ovie Carroll, 2016-11-04). Key findings: hidden 'defaultprinter' service account; smallftpd.exe FTP server (VT 1/72, packed); ftpd.ini with auto_run=1 exposing entire user directory; transfers.log confirming download of temp.zip by 173.73.166.249 (Arlington VA, Verizon FiOS residential) on 2016-06-18T22:21Z; classified documents present on device; 802.11 monitor-mode captures (reconnaissance); Dropbox/Telegram/WhatsApp exfiltration channels. Documents appeared on Chinese university server 2016-06-22/23, four days after FTP transfer. Image has sector errors in E10 (sectors 70565120-70565183, 64 sectors); MD5 unverified; SHA1 verified. CAIE trust degradation applies.

acquisition.note: Live acquisition without write blocker. SHA1 verified by FTK at acquisition time. MD5 fails ewfverify due to sector errors in E10. CAIE trust degradation applies per NIST SP 800-86 §4.3.

artifacts.description: smallftpd.exe found at C:\Users\defaultprinter\smallftpd.exe, SHA-256: 4f1a4c44e268dfb78b8c9a1db6925775925498550e6a717e7576951a076bcd09. VirusTotal 1/72: Jiangmin detects Packed.BDF.en (packed executable). Size 191KB. smallftpd is a legitimate FTP server application repurposed as a covert data exfiltration tool. The binary is packed to evade AV detection. Presence of an FTP server on a corporate-issued research laptop has no legitimate operational justification. The binary was configured to auto-start via ftpd.ini (auto_run=1), establishing persistent exfiltration infrastructure.
provenance_chain: Physical acquisition FTK Imager 2.9 (2016-11-04, examiner Ovie Carroll)

artifacts.description: ftpd.ini configuration file at C:\Users\defaultprinter\ftpd.ini. Critical fields: auto_run=1 (FTP server starts automatically on login), port=21 (standard FTP, unencrypted), user_Login=defaultprinter, user_Password=12345 (intentionally weak), permission_Type_0=LR (list+read, sufficient for exfiltration), directory_Physical_0=C:\Users\PC User (entire Vanko home directory exposed). DynDNS entry (pasv_url=account.dyndns.org) indicates dynamic DNS configured to maintain external accessibility from any network. The username 'defaultprinter' is a social engineering choice designed to appear as a system service account to casual observers. This configuration constitutes a persistent, low-profile data exfiltration channel.
provenance_chain: Physical acquisition FTK Imager 2.9 (2016-11-04, examiner Ovie Carroll)

artifacts.description: transfers.log at C:\Users\defaultprinter\transfers.log. Single entry: '18/06/2016 18:21:49 Download started by defaultprinter [173.73.166.249] : c:\Users\defaultprinter\Desktop\temp.zip' / '18/06/2016 18:21:50 Download completed by defaultprinter : 173.73.166.249'. IP 173.73.166.249 geolocates to Arlington, Virginia (Verizon FiOS residential, AS701). Transfer completed in approximately 1 second. Cross-reference: classified documents appeared on Chinese university server 2016-06-22/23, four days after this transfer. Arlington VA is in the Washington DC metropolitan area, consistent with the Stark Enterprises DC R&D facility location. The 1-second completion time suggests temp.zip was pre-staged and the session was brief and deliberate.
provenance_chain: Physical acquisition FTK Imager 2.9 (2016-11-04, examiner Ovie Carroll)

artifacts.description: Classified Stark Enterprises research documents found on device under C:\Users\defaultprinter\Documents\ and Desktop: (1) 'ZF DNA splice test notes.docx' — zebrafish DNA modification research; (2) 'Rapid cell regeneration research.docx' — rapid cell regeneration drug research; (3) 'calculations on cell regroth.docx' — cell regrowth calculations; (4) 'zebrafish.pdf' — zebrafish research. Corresponding Office temp files (~$) present for multiple documents, indicating they were actively open at or near acquisition time. These documents match exactly the intellectual property described in the Stark Intelligence Division report as having been posted to a Chinese university research file share on 2016-06-22/23. Presence on a personal device outside the StarkResearch server constitutes unauthorized possession of Level 5-8 classified material.

artifacts.description: Hidden user account 'defaultprinter' at C:\Users\defaultprinter\. Account name is a deliberate social engineering choice mimicking a Windows printer service account to avoid detection during casual inspection. The account contains: smallftpd.exe, ftpd.ini, transfers.log, classified documents, Dropbox shortcut, Telegram shortcut, WhatsApp shortcut, NinaResearch folder, NinaResearch.zip, starbucks.csv, security.evtx (copied event log), 7-8-USB-Analysis.pptx. NTUSER.DAT registry confirms user activity on 2016-06-18 at 21:55-22:22Z, coinciding exactly with the FTP transfer (22:21Z). Multiple exfiltration channels present: FTP (smallftpd), cloud storage (Dropbox), encrypted messaging (Telegram, WhatsApp).
provenance_chain: Physical acquisition FTK Imager 2.9 (2016-11-04, examiner Ovie Carroll)

artifacts.description: Two IEEE 802.11 monitor-mode packet captures found at C:\Users\PC User\Documents\: 'starbucks pcap.pcap' (685 packets, 155 seconds, 2016-03-04T17:25Z) and 'testpcap.pcap' (510 packets, 97 seconds, 2016-03-04T17:30Z). Both captured on the same session, 3 months before the June 2016 exfiltration. Radiotap headers confirm promiscuous wireless capture. SSIDs visible: Starbucks WiFi, ATT-WIFI-5250, DRAGONBOY, DaVita-Guest, DaVita-Team, GoWiFi. Capturing network traffic at public WiFi locations with monitor-mode hardware demonstrates advanced technical capability and premeditation. The 3-month gap between capture (March 2016) and exfiltration (June 2016) indicates a deliberate preparation and reconnaissance phase.
provenance_chain: Physical acquisition FTK Imager 2.9 (2016-11-04, examiner Ovie Carroll)

artifacts.description: NTUSER.DAT from defaultprinter account confirms user activity on 2016-06-18 at 21:55:03Z (Snipping Tool, Paint, Notepad, Sticky Notes launched), 21:59:55Z (Google Chrome opened from Desktop shortcut), and 22:22:13Z (File Explorer accessed). FTP transfer log records download completion at 22:21:49Z. Temporal correlation: user was actively operating the machine during the transfer window, browsing with Chrome immediately after. This eliminates the hypothesis that the FTP server was triggered remotely without Vanko's knowledge. The Snipping Tool launch at 21:55Z is consistent with capturing screenshots of classified research content for packaging.
provenance_chain: Physical acquisition FTK Imager 2.9 (2016-11-04, examiner Ovie Carroll)
